question: What does the letter 'M' stand for in the SMART goal framework used in rehabilitation?

options.A: Medical
options.B: Mobile
options.C: Measurable
options.D: Manual

explanation: Goals must be measurable so the healthcare team and the patient can clearly see when a milestone has been reached. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T4#GNS123_U6_T4_h2)

question: At what point in your clinical workflow should healthcare waste be sorted?

options.A: At the final incineration site
options.B: During the weekly municipal garbage collection
options.C: After transport to the central landfill
options.D: Immediately at the point of generation

explanation: Always sort waste right where you use it! Doing it immediately stops dangerous items from getting mixed up with regular trash.

question: What is the very first step in the MBO cycle within a healthcare organization?

options.A: Conducting the final end-of-year staff performance review
options.B: Purchasing new medical equipment for the wards
options.C: Executive leadership defining broad strategic goals
options.D: Punishing departments that failed previous targets

explanation: The MBO process starts at the top, giving a clear direction that individual departments can then break down. [learn more](GST321_U2_T5#GST321_U2_T5_h3)

question: What should you do with the AED pads if the patient suddenly wakes up and starts breathing?

options.A: Move both pads to the patient's back to keep the skin warm
options.B: Peel them off immediately and throw them in the trash
options.C: Leave the pads attached to the chest in case arrest recurs
options.D: Wipe them down with bleach and pack them in the box

explanation: Leave the pads on! A recovered patient can still slip back into cardiac arrest very quickly, and you want the AED ready to go.

question: What is the most important safety rule when changing a patient's tracheostomy neck ties?

options.A: Have an assistant hold the tube in place
options.B: Do it quickly without washing hands
options.C: Inflate the cuff to maximum pressure
options.D: Remove the inner cannula permanently

explanation: Always have a partner hold the tube securely during tie changes. One good cough can pop the tube right out!

question: A male patient insists he doesn't have an STI because his sores don't hurt. How should you gently correct him?

options.A: Painlessness proves that the infection is restricted to the skin surface only
options.B: Some serious infections like syphilis can cause painless sores in their early stages
options.C: If a lesion does not hurt, the body will eliminate the virus automatically
options.D: Painless sores always indicate a non-infectious skin allergy rather than an STI

explanation: It's a common trap! Remind your patients that a lack of pain does not mean lack of disease—syphilis chancres are notorious for being painless.

question: Which layer of the meninges is the tough, outermost layer attached to the skull?

options.A: Choroid plexus
options.B: Arachnoid mater
options.C: Dura mater
options.D: Pia mater

explanation: The dura mater is a thick, durable membrane providing sturdy outer protection for the brain and spinal cord. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h7)

question: Which tool does a nurse grab to take a look inside a patient's ear canal and ear drum?

options.A: An ophthalmoscope
options.B: A tongue depressor
options.C: A stethoscope
options.D: An otoscope

explanation: Spot on! An otoscope has a handy built-in light and magnifier so you can easily check the ear canal and tympanic membrane.

question: What is a very common baby-related issue linked to maternal chronic kidney disease?

options.A: Excessive birth weight
options.B: Fetal bone overgrowth
options.C: Intrauterine growth restriction
options.D: Delayed closure of fontanelles

explanation: Because the placenta gets less nourishment, the baby's growth can slow down inside the womb, leading to low birth weight.

question: A farmer who sprays crops without protection starts feeling dizzy and shaky. What is the likely cause?

options.A: Physical hazard from extreme heat
options.B: Chemical hazard from pesticides
options.C: Ergonomic hazard from heavy lifting
options.D: Biological hazard from soil bacteria

explanation: Pesticides are powerful chemicals that can easily enter the body during spraying and trigger toxic symptoms like dizziness and tremors.

question: Why do very busy hospital wards sometimes lead to unsafe injection practices?

options.A: High patient loads and supply limits tempt staff to rush or cut corners
options.B: New nursing graduates are rarely taught basic injection techniques
options.C: Modern equipment requires electricity that is often unstable
options.D: Patients demand faster injections when waiting rooms are crowded

explanation: True story in many clinics: when resources are tight and too many patients are waiting, pressure mounts. But remember, we must never let stress push us into dangerous shortcuts like reusing gear.

question: In which care delivery model are duties divided strictly by tasks—like one nurse only giving medications and another only doing wound dressings?

options.A: Primary nursing
options.B: Functional nursing
options.C: Team nursing
options.D: Total patient care

explanation: Correct! Functional nursing focuses on getting specific tasks done across all patients, rather than assigning a whole patient to one nurse.

question: When you help a patient with their personal hygiene, why is it considered a special nursing care rather than just a normal house chore?

options.A: It replaces the need to give prescribed drugs
options.B: It is the only duty a nurse can leave for relatives
options.C: It allows the nurse to assess the skin and build trust
options.D: It guarantees the patient will feel zero pain

explanation: Spot on! Washing and grooming put you close enough to spot early skin changes and build a warm, trusting relationship with your patient.

question: A patient calls two days post-procedure reporting mild redness and tenderness. What should you advise?

options.A: Scrape the bandage off and wash the wound with harsh bleach
options.B: Come in immediately for emergency surgical debridement
options.C: Stop all prescribed medications and start strong intravenous antibiotics
options.D: Reassure the patient that mild tenderness is normal, but watch for worsening signs

explanation: You nailed it! A little bit of soreness during healing is totally normal, but we always teach patients what red flags (like pus or spreading redness) to watch out for.

question: After leaving the baby's heart, where does the freshest, most oxygen-rich blood go first?

options.A: Kidneys and adrenal glands
options.B: Lower extremities and feet
options.C: Brain and upper body
options.D: Large and small intestines

explanation: That makes total sense when you think about it: the brain and head need top priority for oxygen to grow rapidly during pregnancy! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h3)

question: A pregnant patient with hyperemesis has low potassium and high blood pH. What is happening?

options.A: Respiratory acidosis
options.B: Metabolic acidosis
options.C: Respiratory alkalosis
options.D: Metabolic alkalosis

explanation: Pumping out stomach acid through continuous vomiting strips the body of hydrogen ions, causing blood pH to rise. That's metabolic alkalosis in action—keep smashing those lab values!

question: You suspect a patient is skipping their blood pressure meds because their readings are still high. How should you start this chat?

options.A: I know you forgot your pills because your blood pressure is still high.
options.B: If you do not start taking your medicine today, you will suffer a stroke.
options.C: Why are you wasting your money by refusing to take your prescribed drugs?
options.D: Many people find it hard to take pills every day; tell me about your routine.

explanation: Brilliant choice! Normalizing the struggle takes away shame and helps the patient open up honestly to you.

question: A patient tells you they are resting at home in their own bed, but they are actually sitting in a hospital ward. How would you describe this?

options.A: Normal cognitive aging changes
options.B: Disorientation to place
options.C: Impaired immediate recall memory
options.D: A defect in cranial nerve function

explanation: When a patient doesn't realize where they physically are, we document it as disorientation to place.

question: Why do midwives and nurses perform Leopold's maneuvers when a mother is admitted?

options.A: To assess fetal lie, presentation, and position
options.B: To check for signs of a postpartum infection
options.C: To measure cervical dilation in centimeters
options.D: To determine the exact gestational age in weeks

explanation: You're doing great! Leopold's maneuvers are simply systematic hand movements on the tummy to figure out how the baby is lying before doing an internal check.

question: What is the main job of progesterone during the second half (luteal phase) of the menstrual cycle?

options.A: To trigger the initial onset of menstrual bleeding
options.B: To cause the breakdown of the corpus luteum
options.C: To prepare the uterine lining for a potential pregnancy
options.D: To stimulate the initial growth of ovarian follicles

explanation: Progesterone turns the inner walls of the womb (the endometrium) into a cozy, nutrient-rich bed, just in case a fertilized egg decides to implant.

question: What does professional accountability primarily require a nurse to do?

options.A: Avoid asking senior doctors for professional guidance
options.B: Cover up small mistakes to prevent hospital lawsuits
options.C: Take responsibility for their clinical actions and decisions
options.D: Work twenty-four-hour shifts without taking a break

explanation: Accountability simply means owning your choices and accepting the professional results of the care you give. We stand tall by our actions! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h6)

question: What simple comfort measure can a nurse suggest for a patient experiencing mild fibroid cramps?

options.A: Applying a heating pad to the lower abdomen
options.B: Drinking large quantities of ice-cold water
options.C: Lying completely flat on the back for hours
options.D: Engaging in high-impact aerobic exercise

explanation: Heat helps relax the tight uterine muscles, offering a wonderful, drug-free way to soothe mild cramping.

question: Your patient suddenly starts wheezing, struggling to breathe, and breaking out in hives right after an IV medication starts. What is your very first action?

options.A: Stop the infusion immediately.
options.B: Slow the infusion rate to a keep-vein-open speed.
options.C: Notify the attending physician before taking action.
options.D: Document the vital signs in the patient chart.

explanation: Brilliant nursing instinct! Always stop the flow first to keep any more of the allergen from entering their system.

question: What is the main drawback of using a 24-hour dietary recall to check a patient's food intake?

options.A: It relies heavily on the patient's memory
options.B: It requires expensive laboratory equipment
options.C: It only measures water and ignores solid food
options.D: It takes over three hours to complete

explanation: Patients easily forget small snacks or misjudge portion sizes when trying to remember everything they ate yesterday.

question: Why does medication given into a muscle absorb faster than medicine given under the skin?

options.A: Muscles are located closer to the outer surface of the skin.
options.B: Intramuscular needles are always made of thinner metal.
options.C: The liver metabolizes intramuscular drugs before they enter blood vessels.
options.D: Muscle tissue has a much richer blood supply than fatty tissue.

explanation: Exactly! Muscles have a bustling network of blood vessels, helping the medication hitch a quick ride into the rest of the body.

question: What is a very common cause of acute (short-term) fatigue?

options.A: A recent viral infection or short-term sleep loss
options.B: Long-standing, unmanaged hypothyroidism
options.C: Advanced autoimmune joint destruction
options.D: A multi-year history of clinical depression

explanation: Exactly! Acute fatigue usually pops up suddenly from something clear and temporary, like fighting off a cold or pulling a late-night reading session for exams.

question: What is 'clinical inertia' when it comes to prescribing medications?

options.A: The rapid changing of medications by multiple different doctors
options.B: The failure of a provider to start or increase therapy when needed
options.C: The delay in pharmacy delivery of critical care drugs
options.D: The complete refusal of a patient to take prescribed pills

explanation: Clinical inertia is just a fancy way of saying healthcare providers sticking to the status quo instead of updating a treatment plan when a patient needs more help.

question: What is the primary focus of palliative care in advanced degenerative disorders?

options.A: Stopping all forms of nursing care
options.B: Curing the genetic disease completely
options.C: Comfort and symptom management
options.D: Increasing rigorous physical therapy

explanation: Palliative care centers on relieving pain and distressing symptoms to ensure the patient remains comfortable and maintains their dignity. Beautiful nursing philosophy!

question: When does the incubation period of an infection officially come to an end?

options.A: The moment the pathogen is fully cleared
options.B: The day the person leaves the hospital
options.C: The appearance of the first clinical symptoms
options.D: The laboratory confirmation of antibodies

explanation: Spot on! The incubation period ends the very moment a patient starts showing signs or symptoms of being sick. You've got this!

question: A patient's chest tube accidentally slips out of the drainage machine. What is your very first nursing move?

options.A: Call the physician immediately before taking action
options.B: Immerse the end of the chest tube in sterile water
options.C: Remove the dressing and inspect the insertion site
options.D: Clamp the chest tube securely with metal hemostats

explanation: Plunging the tube into sterile water instantly recreates a water seal and stops room air from rushing into the chest. Quick thinking saves lives here!

question: What is 'compassion fatigue' in nursing?

options.A: Physical muscle tiredness from standing too long during a shift
options.B: Emotional exhaustion and decreased empathy from continuous exposure to patient suffering
options.C: Boredom caused by doing administrative paperwork all day
options.D: A temporary lack of sleep after working a single night shift

explanation: Compassion fatigue happens when nurses absorb ongoing patient trauma without enough time to recharge, leaving them feeling emotionally drained.

question: Why should a female teen still use condoms even if she is already taking birth control pills?

options.A: Pills do not protect against sexually transmitted infections
options.B: Condoms make hormonal pills absorb faster in the stomach
options.C: Using both methods doubles the hormonal protection level
options.D: Birth control pills stop working if taken without barrier methods

explanation: Exactly! Birth control pills are great for preventing pregnancy, but they do nothing against STIs. Condoms cover that gap. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T12#GNS312_U3_T12_h3)

question: Who takes ultimate responsibility for the surgical procedure?

options.A: The scrub nurse
options.B: The circulating nurse
options.C: The anaesthetist
options.D: The surgeon

explanation: The surgeon leads the team and carries the main legal and clinical responsibility for how the surgery goes. Every team member has a vital role, but the lead surgeon guides the ship!

question: Why do nurses rush to give IV fluids mainly to protect the 'zone of stasis' in a burn?

options.A: It represents the maximum depth of permanent skin and muscle destruction.
options.B: Infection rarely occurs in this specific layer of the burn wound.
options.C: This area is completely insensate and requires immediate surgical removal.
options.D: Tissue in this zone has reduced blood flow and can be saved from necrosis.

explanation: The zone of stasis is bruised and sluggish, but not dead yet! Quick fluids keep blood flowing there so it doesn't cross over into tissue death (necrosis). Great nursing care saves the day!

question: What is the primary underlying assumption of standard precautions?

options.A: Gloves replace the need for washing your hands
options.B: Only visible blood contains dangerous bacterial pathogens
options.C: All body fluids can potentially transmit infectious agents
options.D: Healthy patients require no protective measures at all

explanation: Treating all body fluids as potentially infectious prevents accidental exposure to hidden pathogens. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h3)

question: Why must a nurse check many different body systems when looking out for endocrine disorders?

options.A: Because hormone levels never fluctuate throughout a normal twenty-four-hour day
options.B: Because hormones circulate widely and influence multiple organs and metabolic processes
options.C: Because endocrine glands are all located together in the lower abdominal cavity
options.D: Because nervous system reflexes instantly replace any missing hormone functions

explanation: Hormones travel through the bloodstream touching many organs at once, which is why a single hormone imbalance can cause symptoms all over the body!

question: What is the main way hormonal contraceptives work in the body?

options.A: To speed up the fertilization process in the fallopian tubes
options.B: To mimic natural feedback loops and halt the release of eggs
options.C: To permanently destroy the reproductive organs of a patient
options.D: To increase the natural production of estrogen in the ovaries

explanation: You've got this! Hormonal contraceptives use synthetic hormones to gently trick the body's natural feedback system so that ovulation (releasing an egg) doesn't happen.

question: Why is HIV prevention so crucial in public health?

options.A: There is currently no absolute cure for the infection
options.B: Medications for the virus are too cheap to manufacture
options.C: Patients refuse to take daily medications once diagnosed
options.D: Prevention completely eliminates all other infectious diseases

explanation: Correct! Since a cure isn't here yet, stopping new infections in the first place is our best tool. Keep up the great thinking!

question: Why is 'mixed feeding' (giving both breast milk and other foods or liquids) so risky for a baby born to an HIV-positive mum?

options.A: It completely stops the mother's breast milk production overnight
options.B: It causes immediate allergic reactions in the newborn stomach
options.C: It damages the gut lining and increases the risk of viral transmission
options.D: It neutralizes the protective effect of infant antiretroviral syrups

explanation: Mixing feeds irritates a baby's tiny, developing gut, creating tiny gaps that make it much easier for the virus in breast milk to enter their bloodstream.

question: How do nurses directly help make a hospital Drug Revolving Fund successful?

options.A: By auditing the central bank accounts of the hospital management
options.B: By setting the retail profit markups for all essential medicines
options.C: By importing foreign pharmaceuticals directly from overseas factories
options.D: By providing feedback on drug stock levels and ward consumption

explanation: As nurses, we work directly with patients and medications every day. Spotting low stock early and letting pharmacy know helps keep the supply chain smooth.

question: A patient presents with extreme fatigue, pale skin, and spoon-shaped fingernails. Which deficiency is most likely present?

options.A: Vitamin E
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Thiamine
options.D: Iron

explanation: These are classic signs of iron-deficiency anemia, where reduced hemoglobin levels impair oxygen delivery to tissues. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T9#GNS215_U6_T9_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of a professional nursing organization?

options.A: To protect, advance, and unify the nursing profession
options.B: To provide free medical insurance to members
options.C: To replace state nursing licensing boards
options.D: To handle hospital payroll disputes for all staff

explanation: These organizations exist primarily to uplift the nursing profession as a whole, set standards, and give nurses a collective voice. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T5#GNS112_U1_T5_h1)

question: What type of depression involves mourning the upcoming loss of life and loved ones?

options.A: Reactive and preparatory depression
options.B: Seasonal affective disorder
options.C: Postpartum depression
options.D: Bipolar depressive episodes

explanation: This stage is all about deep sadness for what is being left behind, quietly preparing the heart for the end.

question: How long does the postpartum (puerperium) period typically last for a new mother?

options.A: Six months
options.B: One year
options.C: Six weeks
options.D: Two weeks

explanation: You've got this! The puerperium lasts for about six weeks—this is the special window of time needed for the mother's body and organs to gently return to their pre-pregnancy state.

question: Expired medications and leftover vaccines belong to which waste category?

options.A: Radioactive waste
options.B: Pharmaceutical waste
options.C: Pathological waste
options.D: General domestic waste

explanation: You got it! Drugs and medicines always fall under pharmaceutical waste guidelines. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T2#GNS122_U5_T2_h5)

question: Why are asymptomatic carriers so tricky to deal with during disease outbreaks?

options.A: They develop severe complications that require immediate intensive care unit admission
options.B: They continue normal daily activities and spread the pathogen without knowing they are sick
options.C: They destroy the infection too quickly for laboratory tests to detect any antibodies
options.D: They carry mutated strains of bacteria that are completely immune to all known antibiotics

explanation: Because they don't feel sick, they don't stay home or isolate. They walk around living life normally while unintentionally passing the virus or bacteria along.

question: What physical sign helps a nurse tell a breast abscess apart from simple mastitis?

options.A: Mild tenderness without skin changes
options.B: Absence of any systemic fever
options.C: A distinct, fluctuating, fluid-filled mass
options.D: General warmth across the entire chest

explanation: An abscess forms a walled-off pocket of pus that feels spongy or bouncy (fluctuating) under the fingers. Spot on!

question: What is the primary benefit of choosing the rectal route in clinical practice?

options.A: It guarantees faster absorption than an intravenous injection
options.B: It provides a dependable alternative when oral intake is blocked
options.C: It is the most comfortable method for long-term daily drug use
options.D: It completely eliminates all side effects of strong medications

explanation: Patients who are unconscious or vomiting heavily still need critical medications, making the rectum a practical backup route. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h1)

question: In a healthy adult, about what percentage of total blood volume is made up of plasma?

options.A: Roughly 45 percent
options.B: Roughly 90 percent
options.C: Roughly 55 percent
options.D: Roughly 25 percent

explanation: Great job! Plasma makes up about 55% of your blood, while the remaining 45% is mostly red blood cells.

question: In the RACE fire response steps, what does the letter 'R' stand for?

options.A: Recheck all electrical switches
options.B: Rescue anyone in immediate danger
options.C: Remove oxygen tanks from the building
options.D: Run quickly to the nearest street

explanation: People always come first! The very first priority when a fire starts is getting anyone in danger away from harm.

question: An injured survivor of an assault arrives at your facility. What is your very first clinical priority?

options.A: Conducting a detailed psychological interview
options.B: Filing mandatory police incident reports
options.C: Collecting forensic swabs and clothing fibers
options.D: Stabilizing life-threatening physical injuries

explanation: Saving a life and stabilizing the patient always comes first before collecting evidence or paperwork.

question: Which sign around a skull pin site should ring alarm bells and be reported immediately?

options.A: A small amount of clear dried crusting
options.B: Mild redness that disappears within a day
options.C: Purulent yellow drainage and a foul odor
options.D: Normal skin color around the metal screw

explanation: Pus and bad smells always point to an infection setting in. Let the doctor know right away so it can be treated!

question: How does community health nursing differ from bedside nursing in the hospital?

options.A: It ignores individual patient histories completely
options.B: It requires advanced surgical training for field emergencies
options.C: It deals strictly with paperwork and government health budgets
options.D: It focuses on the collective environment and health of populations

explanation: While bedside nursing cares for one patient at a time, community nursing zooms out to look at whole neighborhoods, environments, and populations!

question: Why might a baby in Gallows traction have trouble breathing deeply?

options.A: The ropes block fresh air from their face
options.B: The sticky tape gives off lung-irritating fumes
options.C: The heavy weights make the room air too thin
options.D: The elevated legs push up on the tummy and limit lung expansion

explanation: Lifting those legs straight up presses the tummy contents against the diaphragm, which can slightly crowd the lungs. Good catch for nursing assessments!

question: What is the normal range for intracranial pressure (ICP) in an adult?

options.A: 80 to 120 mmHg
options.B: 5 to 15 mmHg
options.C: 120 to 140 mmHg
options.D: 30 to 50 mmHg

explanation: Normal ICP stays between 5 and 15 mmHg. This keeps blood flowing nicely to the delicate brain tissues without crushing them.

question: Why is a discharge plan likely to fail if it ignores a patient's home life and financial situation?

options.A: Because medications work better when prescribed without social context
options.B: Because the patient may not be able to afford or follow the recommended instructions at home
options.C: Because nurses are only responsible for care inside the hospital gates
options.D: Because hospital management automatically cancels plans made without doctor approval

explanation: Exactly! If a care plan doesn't fit what the patient can actually afford or do at home, they won't be able to stick to it.

question: Why do nurses apply a cotton stockinette and padding before wrapping the plaster rolls?

options.A: To add bright color and decoration to the finished cast
options.B: To help the wet plaster dry much faster from the inside
options.C: To protect the underlying skin from irritation and pressure
options.D: To prevent the limb from shrinking inside the hard cast

explanation: Padding acts as a cozy cushion between the hard plaster and bony areas, keeping the skin safe from sores.

question: What is a major transport-related challenge that often contributes to maternal deaths in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive availability of fully equipped ambulances in villages
options.B: Too many doctors available at primary healthcare centers
options.C: Delays in transportation and reaching a medical facility
options.D: Immediate acceptance of patients at tertiary hospitals

explanation: Getting stuck trying to find transport to a hospital (the famous 'second delay') is a huge hurdle in saving mothers in remote areas.

question: Why are people with long-term leg swelling at higher risk for skin infections like cellulitis?

options.A: Swollen legs attract insects that transmit bacterial infections.
options.B: Increased blood flow carries too many white blood cells to the skin.
options.C: Fluid buildup inside the tissues directly manufactures harmful bacteria.
options.D: Stretched, fragile skin easily develops cracks that let bacteria enter.

explanation: Exactly! When skin is constantly stretched out by fluid, it gets dry, thin, and fragile. Tiny cracks form easily, giving bacteria an easy doorway in.

question: A patient on a breathing machine (ventilator) is at high risk for which mouth problem?

options.A: Losing their sense of smell completely and forever
options.B: Sudden growth of wisdom teeth right at the back
options.C: Drooling because of too much natural saliva production
options.D: Fast plaque buildup and ventilator-associated pneumonia

explanation: You've got this! Because intubated patients cannot clean their own teeth and often have dry mouths, germs gather quickly and can travel down to cause pneumonia.

question: When does everyday worry cross the line into a clinical anxiety disorder?

options.A: Normal worry only occurs in children and teenagers.
options.B: Normal worry never causes physical symptoms like a racing heart.
options.C: Clinical anxiety persists excessively and disrupts daily functioning.
options.D: Clinical anxiety disappears immediately once a stressor is removed.

explanation: We all worry about exams or finances sometimes! But clinical anxiety hangs around stubbornly and makes it hard to get through daily life. Spotting this difference helps you understand when a patient truly needs support.

question: Why does giving out too much informal credit to patients hurt a DRF?

options.A: It encourages manufacturers to stop producing generic medicines
options.B: It causes all the drugs in the pharmacy warehouse to expire faster
options.C: It forces the government to increase taxes on medical supplies
options.D: It creates cash flow gaps that prevent timely restocking of medicines

explanation: When money is stuck as 'owed bills', the pharmacy drawers are empty. Without cash on hand, suppliers won't send new stock.

question: What is the main reason for doing a pre-placement medical examination?

options.A: To test physical strength for office roles
options.B: To determine retirement pension packages
options.C: To provide immediate treatment for interview injuries
options.D: To establish a baseline health status before a worker begins a job

explanation: Correct! Pre-placement exams give you a clear starting point of the worker's health so you can notice if the job affects them later.

question: A patient with a fresh neck injury suddenly has dangerously low blood pressure and zero reflexes. What is this temporary condition called?

options.A: Renal failure
options.B: Cerebral edema
options.C: Tetraplegic fever
options.D: Spinal shock

explanation: Spot on! Spinal shock happens right after a severe spinal cord injury. The cord basically goes to 'sleep' temporarily, causing a sudden loss of all reflexes and muscle tone below the injury site.

question: What is one of the most important daily fluid instructions to give a patient managing gout?

options.A: Drink plenty of water daily
options.B: Only drink liquids during mealtimes
options.C: Avoid water and drink soda instead
options.D: Restrict all fluids to prevent swelling

explanation: Correct! Drinking lots of water helps the kidneys flush out extra uric acid before it has a chance to form stubborn crystals.

question: A patient with a history of heavy drinking stumbles when walking and has jerky eye movements. What should you suspect?

options.A: An epileptic seizure
options.B: Acute appendicitis
options.C: Diabetic ketoacidosis
options.D: Wernicke encephalopathy

explanation: Spot on! Stumbling, eye issues, and a history of heavy drinking are textbook signs of Wernicke encephalopathy.

question: Which of these is a dangerous and incorrect practice with disposable medical gloves?

options.A: Cleaning your hands before putting them on
options.B: Choosing nitrile instead of latex
options.C: Washing and reusing them between patients
options.D: Changing them after every single patient

explanation: Disposable gloves are strictly single-use! Washing them ruins their protective barrier and spreads germs around the ward.

question: A patient agrees they are sick, stays home from classes, and asks family members if they look feverish. Which stage of illness is this?

options.A: Assumption of the sick role
options.B: Recovery and rehabilitation
options.C: Symptom experience
options.D: Dependent-patient role

explanation: When you step back from your daily duties and look for validation from loved ones that you need rest, you've entered the sick role.

question: Why does the anaesthetist stay close to the patient's head during surgery?

options.A: To assist the surgeon with knot-tying and tissue retraction
options.B: To manage the airway and monitor breathing continuously
options.C: To clean blood off the surgical instruments during the operation
options.D: To count surgical instruments before the wound is closed

explanation: By staying right by the head, the anaesthetist can easily keep the airway open, give oxygen, and watch vital signs every second.

question: What goes wrong in hyperproliferative skin conditions like psoriasis?

options.A: Skin cells multiply much faster than normal and pile up on the surface
options.B: Melanocytes completely disappear from the deepest layer of the dermis
options.C: Sebaceous glands shut down, leaving the skin completely dry and scaly
options.D: Skin cells stop growing entirely, causing deep chronic ulcerations

explanation: Well done! In conditions like psoriasis, cells grow way too fast, creating those thick, raised patches on the skin.

question: When giving ear drops to an adult, how should you pull the ear pinna?

options.A: Downward and forward
options.B: Downward and backward
options.C: Straight outward
options.D: Upward and backward

explanation: Great clinical technique! For adults, pulling the pinna upward and backward straightens out that curvy ear canal so your drops flow smoothly down to the eardrum.

question: Which specialist should you call to trim the toenails of a patient with advanced diabetic foot complications?

options.A: A general ward nurse
options.B: A physical therapist
options.C: A hospital pharmacist
options.D: A podiatrist

explanation: Spot on! Podiatrists are foot experts trained to safely handle high-risk nail and skin care for patients with poor circulation or nerve issues.

question: What do luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) directly do to the gonads?

options.A: Stopping the secretion of growth hormone during sleep
options.B: Shutting down the pituitary gland through negative feedback
options.C: Stimulating the production of sex steroids like estrogen and testosterone
options.D: Directly causing the closure of the epiphyseal plates in long bones

explanation: Great job! LH and FSH act like messengers to the ovaries and testes, telling them to start producing sex hormones.

question: Which of these is NOT a major challenge currently facing the nursing profession worldwide?

options.A: Managing chronic non-communicable diseases
options.B: Complete elimination of all patient illnesses
options.C: Shortages of qualified nursing personnel
options.D: High rates of workplace stress and burnout

explanation: We haven't wiped out all illnesses yet! Instead, nurses worldwide battle daily with staff shortages, burnout, and rising chronic illnesses.

question: What is a major risk of using strong steroid creams on the skin for too long?

options.A: Permanent darkening of the skin to a deep black color
options.B: Skin thinning and atrophy at the application site
options.C: Complete numbness and loss of feeling in the treated limb
options.D: Rapid overgrowth of thick hair across the entire body

explanation: You got it! Overusing strong topical steroids can weaken the skin, making it thin, fragile, and prone to stretch marks.

question: Why is knowing a drug's class super helpful when you meet an unfamiliar medication on the ward?

options.A: It tells the nurse the exact room temperature for storing the drug
options.B: It guarantees the patient will not experience any adverse reactions
options.C: It gives immediate clues about expected effects and side effects
options.D: It eliminates the need to check the hospital dosage calculations

explanation: Drugs in the same family share similar actions and side effects. Once you know the class, you already know a lot about how it behaves!

question: What does a regular B-Mode ultrasound show you on the screen?

options.A: A bright color map of bone strength
options.B: A two-dimensional greyscale picture of internal organs
options.C: A live wave graph of the heart's electrical rhythm
options.D: A 3D heat map of the body's temperature

explanation: Think of B-Mode as your standard black-and-white anatomical view that outlines the shape and structure of organs.

question: Which action shows that you are using good body mechanics while making a bed?

options.A: Keeping the hospital bed in its lowest position throughout the procedure
options.B: Stretching your arms far across the mattress without moving your feet
options.C: Using leg muscles with a wide base of support when moving heavy items
options.D: Twisting rapidly at the waist to transfer linen from one hand to the other

explanation: Wonderful! Using your legs and keeping a wide stance protects your back from injury during nursing duties.

question: How did the role of the nurse change with the introduction of coronary care units?

options.A: Nurses were trained to independently spot dangerous rhythms and start emergency defibrillation
options.B: Nurses handed over all emergency response duties entirely to specialized physicians
options.C: Nurses focused solely on administering oral medications prescribed at shift change
options.D: Nurses were restricted from touching cardiac monitors without direct written doctor orders

explanation: Because cardiac arrest happens instantly, CCU nurses had to be trained to act immediately without waiting for a physician. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why are two different medications used together in a medical abortion?

options.A: Combining them achieves a higher success rate than using either drug by itself
options.B: Using both drugs simultaneously shortens the bleeding duration by half
options.C: The second drug is needed immediately to reverse the side effects of the first
options.D: Mifepristone causes the contractions while misoprostol blocks the hormones

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! Using mifepristone first to prepare the uterus and then misoprostol to empty it works best together for a complete process.

question: How can a nurse check if a patient truly understands how to take their new medicine?

options.A: Handing them a dense medical textbook to read overnight in bed
options.B: Asking a family member to sign a legal compliance waiver
options.C: Assuming they understand if they nod silently during the talk
options.D: Asking the patient to repeat the instructions back in their own words

explanation: The 'teach-back' method is a nursing favorite! Having them explain it back in plain words guarantees they actually got the message.

question: Why do primary blood disorders often stress multiple organs in the body?

options.A: Because bone marrow overproduction causes physical pressure in the abdomen
options.B: Because blood circulates through every organ and delivers vital oxygen and nutrients
options.C: Because white blood cells directly attack healthy organ tissues
options.D: Because plasma proteins constantly bind to waste products

explanation: Since blood travels to every single corner of your body, any problem in the blood means every organ misses out on the oxygen and food it needs. It's a chain reaction!

question: Which of the following is NOT a major challenge to population policy implementation in Nigeria?

options.A: Cultural and religious beliefs favoring large family sizes
options.B: Universal access to fully funded and equipped rural clinics
options.C: Inadequate funding and poor health infrastructure
options.D: Political instability and shifting government priorities

explanation: Sadly, fully funded and equipped rural clinics are far from universal in Nigeria! Most rural clinics actually struggle with shortages, making this option the false statement.

question: Which germ causes leprosy?

options.A: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
options.B: Streptococcus pyogenes
options.C: Mycobacterium leprae
options.D: Treponema pallidum

explanation: Spot on! Leprosy is caused by Mycobacterium leprae. It loves to hang out in cooler parts of the body like the skin and outer nerves.

question: Why does staring at a phone late at night make it hard for teenagers to sleep?

options.A: Blue light suppresses melatonin production and delays the sleep cycle
options.B: The physical weight of a smartphone makes the mattress uncomfortable
options.C: Reading text messages increases the body temperature above normal limits
options.D: Electromagnetic waves from Wi-Fi routers destroy sleep-related hormones

explanation: The blue light from screens tricks our brains into thinking the sun is still up, which blocks melatonin (the hormone that tells our body it's time to rest).

question: What is the primary function of a bed cradle?

options.A: To elevate swollen legs above heart level
options.B: To keep the patient in a sitting upright posture
options.C: To prevent the patient from rolling out of bed
options.D: To lift the weight of blankets off the patient's body

explanation: A bed cradle creates a protective arch that keeps heavy bed linens from pressing directly against sensitive skin or wounds. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T4#GNS112_U4_T4_h3)

question: Why is the VAPP Act's stance on marital rape considered a major legal milestone in Nigeria?

options.A: It recognizes that sexual assault can occur within a marriage.
options.B: It requires marriage counseling before any wedding takes place.
options.C: It gives husbands full legal ownership over their spouses.
options.D: It bans marriage for individuals under the age of forty.

explanation: Spot on! Older laws did not criminalize forced sexual acts between spouses, making this a massive step forward for human rights and safety.

question: How can cultural beliefs negatively impact a community's health status if ignored by health workers?

options.A: The birth rate might increase without affecting disease transmission
options.B: The local government might run out of financial grants for road construction
options.C: Weather patterns could shift and cause unexpected droughts
options.D: People may avoid formal health facilities and rely on harmful traditional practices

explanation: When health workers ignore cultural beliefs, patients often reject modern treatment in favor of familiar traditions, leading to delayed care and worse health outcomes. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h5)

question: Which brain structure acts as the ultimate master control center for the autonomic nervous system?

options.A: Hypothalamus
options.B: Cerebellum
options.C: Thalamus
options.D: Occipital lobe

explanation: The hypothalamus is the boss! It coordinates all visceral signals to keep your internal environment (homeostasis) stable and balanced.

question: Which statement best describes the role of multidisciplinary rounds in preventing complications?

options.A: It gives doctors a chance to give orders without listening to nursing staff.
options.B: Different healthcare professionals share expertise to catch risks from multiple angles.
options.C: It ensures that family members make all medical decisions.
options.D: It replaces the need for continuous bedside monitoring machines.

explanation: When nurses, pharmacists, therapists, and doctors talk together, they spot overlapping problems that one person working alone might easily miss. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h7)

question: What should you do immediately if a patient shows signs of pain while their arm is being moved?

options.A: Continue moving faster to get past the painful spot
options.B: Ask a relative to hold the arm down so you can finish
options.C: Stop the exercise right away and check the joint
options.D: Ignore it because passive exercise always hurts

explanation: Pain is your stop sign! It tells you something is being over-stretched or injured. Always pause and assess.

question: What usually causes antimicrobial resistance to spread in clinical practice?

options.A: Using combination drug therapy for mycobacterial infections
options.B: Regular handwashing and proper cleaning of hospital equipment
options.C: Administering culture-guided targeted therapy to patients
options.D: Inappropriate use and incomplete courses of anti-infective drugs

explanation: Misusing antibiotics—like taking them for viral colds or stopping halfway—teaches bacteria how to survive our best drugs. Good hand hygiene and smart prescribing protect everyone!

question: Why is it best to use short, simple sentences when talking to a patient in a full-blown panic attack?

options.A: Short sentences prevent the nurse from becoming overly anxious as well.
options.B: Patients with panic disorders have difficulty hearing long words.
options.C: Simple sentences make the patient fall asleep immediately.
options.D: Patients in panic have impaired cognitive processing and cannot handle complex information.

explanation: When panic takes over, the brain is flooded with fear and cannot process long explanations. Keep your words brief, clear, and easy to digest.

question: A nurse assesses an adult patient with suspected acute osteomyelitis. Which set of findings is most expected?

options.A: Yellowing of the eyes, dark urine, and severe abdominal cramping
options.B: High fever, localized bone pain, swelling, and extreme tenderness
options.C: Numbness in both hands, low blood pressure, and a dry cough
options.D: Painless joint stiffness, dry skin, and generalized hair loss

explanation: Acute osteomyelitis classically triggers both systemic signs of infection like fever and distinct local signs like pain, warmth, and swelling at the bone site. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h5)

question: Which cells in the stomach lining make hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor?

options.A: Parietal cells
options.B: Mucous neck cells
options.C: G cells
options.D: Chief cells

explanation: Spot on! Parietal cells are the stomach's acid factories. They also make intrinsic factor, which your body needs to absorb vitamin B12 properly.

question: A nurse fills out a Yellow Form for a patient who got a rash after taking two new drugs and an herbal supplement. What should be included in the medication history?

options.A: Only document the drug that the nurse personally administered
options.B: List all prescribed drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal products
options.C: Ignore the herbal supplement since it is not a pharmaceutical drug
options.D: Only list the most expensive brand-name prescription drug

explanation: Always list everything! Herbal remedies and over-the-counter items frequently cause or contribute to adverse reactions.

question: How is a true drug allergy different from a general adverse drug reaction (ADR)?

options.A: ADRs only affect the skin, whereas allergies affect internal organs.
options.B: ADRs are predictable, but allergies are completely impossible to track.
options.C: Allergies involve the immune system, while ADRs can happen through other body processes.
options.D: Allergies always require surgery, while ADRs never do.

explanation: Think of it this way: all allergies are a type of ADR, but allergies specifically trigger your immune system, while other ADRs can happen through normal body chemistry.

question: What hormone must be released by a developing embryo to keep the corpus luteum alive?

options.A: Thyroid-stimulating hormone
options.B: Testosterone
options.C: Human chorionic gonadotropin
options.D: Luteinizing hormone

explanation: Embryonic human chorionic gonadotropin signals the corpus luteum not to degenerate, ensuring continued hormone support for the pregnancy. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h6)

question: Why do we perform passive range of motion exercises for a paralyzed patient?

options.A: To keep joints flexible and stop them from getting stiff
options.B: To replace the need for turning the client in bed
options.C: To help the nervous system grow new nerves
options.D: To build big muscles in the affected arms and legs

explanation: Since paralyzed muscles cannot move on their own, moving the joints passively stops them from freezing up or developing tight contractures. You've got this!

question: How is terminal (palliative) sedation different from physician-assisted suicide?

options.A: Patient consent is never required for terminal sedation procedures
options.B: Terminal sedation is performed by family members instead of doctors
options.C: Terminal sedation always shortens the patient's lifespan significantly
options.D: The intent of terminal sedation is to relieve unbearable pain, not to cause death

explanation: The main goal here is purely comfort and pain relief. Even if the heavy medicine makes the patient sleep deeply, the goal is never to cause death.

question: Why is it important to empty and wash a urinal right after a patient uses it?

options.A: It is required before the patient is allowed to drink more water
options.B: It prevents accidental spills and unpleasant odors in the patient room
options.C: It ensures the plastic material does not melt near the bed
options.D: It stops the patient from producing too much urine overnight

explanation: Leaving a full urinal around is an accident waiting to happen—plus, nobody wants a smelly ward room! Prompt clearing keeps the environment fresh and safe.

question: You need to draw routine blood from a patient who has an IV line running in their left forearm. What should you do?

options.A: Use a butterfly needle to draw blood from the hand on the same side
options.B: Draw the blood specimen from the opposite uninfused arm
options.C: Turn off the intravenous infusion for two minutes and draw from above the site
options.D: Draw the sample directly through the running intravenous catheter

explanation: Always avoid drawing blood from an arm with an active IV. The IV fluids will dilute your sample and give you completely inaccurate lab numbers!

question: Which part of the body is the main organ for managing heat exchange with the environment?

options.A: The kidneys
options.B: The lungs
options.C: The skin
options.D: The liver

explanation: You got this! The skin is our outer boundary, making it our primary tool for releasing or trapping body heat.

question: Which body feature makes female patients more likely to get a catheter-related urinary tract infection?

options.A: A wider urethral opening
options.B: A larger bladder capacity than males
options.C: An absence of a muscular sphincter
options.D: A shorter urethra close to the anal opening

question: Why does a lack of basic education often lead to higher rates of unintended pregnancies?

options.A: It guarantees employment in high-stress urban environments
options.B: It increases the biological fertility rate of every woman
options.C: It physically alters the organs of the reproductive system
options.D: It limits access to accurate information on how to prevent conception

explanation: Exactly! Without proper education, people are left relying on myths instead of solid facts about family planning.

question: Which of these statements is FALSE regarding legal accountability in drug administration?

options.A: A nurse is completely free from liability if a doctor wrote the incorrect order
options.B: A nurse can lose their nursing license for gross negligence in medication handling
options.C: A nurse is legally responsible for verifying every drug before giving it
options.D: A nurse must follow facility policies and state scope of practice laws

explanation: You can't just blame the doctor! Nurses share legal accountability and cannot blindly give a harmful drug just because it was prescribed.

question: A patient is getting a CT scan with contrast dye for an adrenal tumor. What is a vital nursing check beforehand?

options.A: Measuring the patient's 24-hour urine cortisol
options.B: Checking for allergies to iodine or shellfish
options.C: Testing the patient for active thyroid antibodies
options.D: Ensuring the patient has swallowed radioactive iodine

question: What long-term issue can happen if severe uterine infections leave behind scar tissue?

options.A: Complete loss of bladder control
options.B: Infertility or menstrual problems
options.C: Enlargement of the external genitalia
options.D: Permanent cessation of all hormones

question: A test report shows extremely high acid output and multiple stomach ulcers. Which condition does this suggest?

options.A: Zollinger-Ellison syndrome
options.B: Chronic atrophic gastritis
options.C: Pyloric valve stenosis
options.D: Pernicious anemia

question: What is a major challenge health workers face when trying to eradicate disease reservoirs?

options.A: Poor coordination between human health and veterinary agencies
options.B: Immediate compliance from all community members during campaigns
options.C: Excessive funding that leads to unspent public health budgets
options.D: An overabundance of trained environmental health personnel

explanation: That's right! Controlling animal-borne diseases needs teamwork between doctors and veterinarians, but communication gaps can slow things down.

question: What is the big danger if you fail to mix a diluted lotion thoroughly?

options.A: Extending the expiration date by several months
options.B: Turning the entire mixture into a watery liquid
options.C: Creating concentrated hot spots that irritate the skin
options.D: Changing the color of the cream to bright yellow

explanation: If you don't mix it well, pockets of high-strength medicine can hide in the cream and sting the patient's skin.

question: A woman carrying twins at 38 weeks asks to have her babies at home. What should you tell her?

options.A: Suggest waiting until labor is well established before deciding
options.B: Explain that multiple pregnancies require hospital care due to higher risks
options.C: Encourage home birth because twins are common in the community

explanation: Great clinical thinking! Twin pregnancies carry higher chances of tricky presentations or heavy bleeding, so they truly need the safety of a health facility.

question: Why do doctors order a D-dimer blood test when checking for a deep vein thrombosis (DVT)?

options.A: To look for protein fragments that show a recent blood clot is breaking down
options.B: To measure blood pressure inside leg veins
options.C: To see plaque buildup inside the aorta
options.D: To check how fast red blood cells settle in a tube

explanation: D-dimer is a leftover protein piece that floats around when the body is dissolving a blood clot. If the test is negative, it's a great clue that a clot isn't lurking there!

question: What is the medical term for an infection of the middle ear?

options.A: Otitis externa

question: How long should you rub your hands together when using an alcohol-based hand rub?

question: A patient on warfarin for a heart condition starts taking a daily garlic supplement. What is the major concern here?

options.A: The combination can significantly increase the risk of bleeding
options.B: The warfarin will turn the garlic tablets into poison
options.C: The patient will develop severe vitamin C toxicity

question: What is the main legal risk if a nurse forgets to document a medication right after giving it?

options.A: The hospital computer system will delete the patient file

options.C: The patient's insurance company will refuse to pay the bill

question: What is the primary definition of gender-based violence?

options.A: Physical fights that happen between family members inside the home
options.B: Bullying that occurs exclusively in school or workplace environments
options.C: Any harmful act directed against someone based on differences between males and females
options.D: Any aggressive behavior shown by a healthcare worker to a patient

question: Why is emotional support such a big part of nursing care after an abortion or miscarriage?

options.A: Emotional counseling completely eliminates the risk of physical infection
options.B: Patients often experience complex grief, anxiety, and psychological distress
options.C: Psychological support replaces the need for vital sign monitoring
options.D: Hormonal changes only affect physical health and never mental well-being

explanation: Losing a pregnancy hurts deeply on the inside. Being a warm, listening nurse is just as important as checking physical vitals!

question: Why does long-term low blood oxygen sometimes lead to secondary polycythemia?

options.A: The liver releases clotting factors to repair damaged alveolar walls

options.C: The body tries to carry more oxygen by making extra red blood cells
options.D: Dehydrated blood vessels concentrate the existing red blood cells rapidly

question: What sign would you most expect in a patient with a low platelet count?

options.A: Stiff neck and high fever spikes

options.C: Petechiae and bleeding gums
options.D: Yellow discoloration of the sclera

explanation: Platelets help us stop bleeding. When they're low, tiny red spots (petechiae) or bleeding gums show us that clotting isn't happening properly.

question: How does early Pick's disease usually look different from Alzheimer's disease?

options.A: Alzheimer's disease exclusively affects people under age fifty.

options.C: Pick's disease alters behavior and personality first rather than memory.

question: A patient scheduled for a small skin biopsy is panicking because they are sure it means they have cancer. How should the nurse reply?

options.A: Confirm that the doctor strongly suspects a malignant tumor

options.D: Explain that biopsies are done to check many different conditions, not just cancer

question: What is a cardiovascular complication?

options.A: A side effect caused by taking too many vitamins
options.B: A normal reaction to doing heavy exercise
options.C: A brand new primary heart disease
options.D: A secondary problem that happens after initial heart or blood vessel damage

explanation: Think of a complication as a follow-up problem. When the heart or blood vessels are already damaged, other issues pop up because the body's normal coping systems get overwhelmed. You've got this!

question: How does severe dehydration affect the skin?

options.A: It permanently changes the natural pigmentation of the skin
options.B: It speeds up the healing rate of minor skin abrasions
options.C: It causes an overproduction of natural skin oils
options.D: It reduces blood flow and impairs cellular metabolism

question: Which common bacterium is most often linked to duodenal ulcers?

options.A: Escherichia coli

options.C: Helicobacter pylori

question: What is the main job of the body's immune system when it comes to body tissues?

options.A: To destroy the body's own healthy cells
options.B: To distinguish between self and non-self
options.C: To produce energy for cellular repair
options.D: To circulate red blood cells through tissue

explanation: Spot on! The immune system's core superpower is knowing the difference between what belongs to your body (self) and foreign invaders (non-self).

question: A patient in Buck's extension says their heel feels like it is burning under the foam boot. What is your best immediate action?

options.A: Inspect the skin under the boot for redness or pressure damage
options.B: Permanently cut off the traction straps without telling anyone

question: What serious physical problem often happens in the late stage of Alzheimer's?

options.A: Sudden and rapid weight gain from fluid retention

options.C: Excessive bone growth in the lower extremities
options.D: Swallowing difficulties leading to aspiration risk

question: A client comes to the clinic asking for a reversible method that lasts for several years without her needing to remember it daily. Which option fits best?

options.A: Periodic calendar rhythm tracking with her partner
options.B: Combined oral contraceptive pills taken every morning
options.C: An intrauterine device inserted into the uterine cavity

question: What is the biggest danger of pulling a Guinea worm out too fast?

options.A: The worm may snap, causing severe inflammation and infection
options.B: The patient will instantly lose consciousness from shock
options.C: The infection will immediately spread to other family members
options.D: The remaining worm will travel directly to the patient's heart

question: What complication can happen if large amounts of plain tap water are used for lavage in young children?

options.A: Instant calcification of leftover food particles inside the gut

options.C: Sudden spikes in blood pressure throughout the body

question: What lifestyle tip should you give a patient who keeps waking up all night to urinate (nocturia)?

question: A patient asks you (the nurse) to hang out after they leave the hospital. Why is this a bad idea?

question: How long should you listen with a stethoscope to confirm a patient has no heart sounds?

question: Which of the following is considered a primary biological data source for disease confirmation?

question: What is the main difference between nursing malpractice and ordinary negligence?

options.A: Malpractice only happens when a patient dies in the ICU

options.C: Malpractice involves specialized professional skills and breaches of professional standards

question: Why do many patients feel shoulder pain shortly after laparoscopic gallbladder surgery?

options.A: Trapped carbon dioxide gas irritating the phrenic nerve
options.B: Muscle strain from lifting heavy things too early
options.C: Infection in the shoulder joint from bad positioning
