question: Why is putting in a large-bore intravenous (IV) line such an urgent priority when managing severe PPH?

options.A: To provide a pathway for total parenteral nutrition
options.B: To make it easy to give routine pain relief
options.C: To allow rapid running of IV fluids and blood products
options.D: To monitor central venous pressure continuously

explanation: When a mother is losing blood quickly, every second counts. Wide IV lines let you pump in lifesaving fluids and blood fast enough to beat shock.

question: Why does a person feel breathless when there is a mismatch in breathing signals?

options.A: The brain gets confused because the effort of trying to breathe doesn't match how the lungs actually move.
options.B: The brainstem shuts down ventilation to conserve oxygen.
options.C: The diaphragm relaxes completely and refuses to contract further.
options.D: The heart pumps too much blood to the lungs, causing fluid overload.

explanation: Breathlessness happens when the brain's command to breathe doesn't match the actual movement of the chest wall. Simple and clear!

question: Which of these everyday lifestyle habits can negatively impact fertility in both men and women?

options.A: Natural age-related decline
options.B: Genetic chromosome makeup
options.C: Congenital uterine anomalies
options.D: Cigarette smoking

explanation: Brilliant! Smoking is a habit patients can actually change, and it directly hurts both sperm quality and ovarian health. You're mastering this!

question: Which internal organ is frequently damaged alongside the joints in untreated chronic gout?

options.A: The brain
options.B: The spleen
options.C: The kidneys
options.D: The lungs

explanation: Keep this in mind! High uric acid doesn't just affect joints; it can also form kidney stones or damage renal tissue over time.

question: Why is taking off your PPE in the correct, specific order so important?

options.A: To ensure the equipment can be washed and reused for the next shift
options.B: To prevent transferring trapped pathogens from the gear onto your skin
options.C: To prevent the plastic straps from snapping during disposal
options.D: To speed up the process so you can leave the isolation room faster

explanation: The outside of your PPE is covered in germs. If you take it off carelessly, you'll end up wiping those germs right onto your face or hands!

question: You are wrapping up an admission chat with a new patient. Which action belongs to the termination phase?

options.A: Observing the patient's non-verbal body language closely
options.B: Summarizing key findings and outlining the next steps
options.C: Asking open-ended questions about childhood medical history
options.D: Introducing yourself and explaining your nursing role

explanation: You nailed it! The termination phase is simply wrapping things up, recapping what was discussed, and telling them what happens next.

question: A client wants a refill for her birth control, but admits she might already be pregnant. What should you do first?

options.A: Perform a pregnancy test before giving the refill
options.B: Tell her to double her dose for the next week
options.C: Switch her to a progestin-only pill right away
options.D: Refill the prescription immediately without questions

explanation: Safety first! Always rule out an existing pregnancy before continuing hormonal contraceptives to protect both the client and potential pregnancy.

question: Why do we call patient assessment in the intensive care unit a continuous loop?

options.A: Because vital signs never change in stable patients
options.B: Because doctors only visit patients once a day
options.C: Because hospital computers demand hourly data entry
options.D: Because interventions require constant re-evaluation

explanation: Think of it as a cycle: you assess, you act, and then you immediately check how the patient responded. It keeps repeating to keep them safe!

question: Which of these is NOT one of the safety rules for giving medications?

options.A: Right patient identity
options.B: Right dosage amount
options.C: Right drug name
options.D: Right room decoration

explanation: Haha, room decor won't help your patient! We stick to the vital rights like right patient, drug, dose, route, and time.

question: What is the main reason for inserting the needle below the L2 vertebra?

options.A: To avoid injuring the main spinal cord
options.B: To bypass the thick muscles of the back
options.C: To prevent leakage of blood from veins
options.D: To reach the heart valves more easily

explanation: Exactly! Since the spinal cord ends around L1-L2, sticking the needle lower keeps the delicate central nervous tissue safe from harm.

question: Why is correct waste segregation at the primary healthcare level so critical?

options.A: It makes the clinic storeroom look neat for visiting supervisors
options.B: It ensures that general waste burns at a much lower temperature
options.C: It protects community waste handlers from accidental injuries and infections
options.D: It allows the clinic to recycle all used plastic syringes into new toys

explanation: Proper sorting ensures that hazardous items like needles and blood-soaked cotton do not end up in municipal dumps where they can harm the public. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h6)

question: Why do close contacts of a meningitis patient get given preventive (prophylactic) antibiotics?

options.A: To cut down hospital bills in the community
options.B: To clear the bacteria from their nose and throat and stop it from spreading
options.C: To cure unrelated infections they might have
options.D: To boost their immunity against all viruses

explanation: Giving quick preventive meds to family members or close contacts clears the bacteria out of their upper airway before it can make them sick or pass it to someone else.

question: Which nursing action helps prevent joint stiffness (contractures) in a patient on bed rest?

options.A: Restricting fluid intake to reduce swelling
options.B: Keeping the bed locked in a flat position all day
options.C: Performing range-of-motion exercises regularly
options.D: Applying ice packs to every major joint

explanation: Moving joints gently through their full range keeps muscles and tendons flexible and stops them from tightening up permanently.

question: What is a common long-term physical problem caused by having very heavy periods for a long time?

options.A: Permanent kidney failure
options.B: Iron-deficiency anemia
options.C: Broken bones
options.D: Severe adult asthma

explanation: You nailed it! Losing blood month after month empties out the body's iron reserves, leading directly to anemia.

question: Why should a nurse remind the team to periodically release a retractor during a long operation?

options.A: To allow the metal joints to cool down from body heat
options.B: To clean off accumulated blood and keep the instrument shiny
options.C: To prevent tissue damage and lack of blood supply from constant pressure
options.D: To change the size of the wound opening as the surgery progresses

explanation: Continuous heavy retraction can cut off blood flow to the edges of the wound, leading to localized tissue death. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h6)

question: Why do doctors frequently prescribe ACE inhibitors or ARBs for chronic glomerulonephritis?

options.A: They replace the function of dialysis
options.B: They cure bacterial bladder infections instantly
options.C: They lower pressure inside the glomeruli and reduce protein loss
options.D: They stimulate the bone marrow to make red blood cells

explanation: These medications relax the tiny blood vessels leaving the kidney filters, which drops the pressure inside and protects the remaining nephrons from wearing out.

question: What should you do right away if your patient feels sharp belly cramps while you are running the fluid?

options.A: Stop the flow immediately until the cramp passes
options.B: Ignore the symptom as a normal expected reaction
options.C: Raise the fluid container higher to finish quickly
options.D: Push the rectal tube deeper into the sigmoid colon

explanation: Cramping means the bowel is filling up too fast! Always pause the flow and let the patient relax before starting again.

question: Why do young children with sickle cell anaemia take daily preventive penicillin?

options.A: To thin the blood and stop red blood cells from clumping together
options.B: To stimulate the bone marrow to create more red blood cells
options.C: To lower the body temperature and prevent sudden high fevers
options.D: To protect against severe infections caused by functional asplenia

explanation: Over time, sickle cell damage makes the spleen stop working well (functional asplenia). Because the spleen is vital for fighting certain bacteria, daily penicillin acts as a shield to keep these kids safe from severe infections.

question: What is a vital safety item a patient living with diabetes should always carry around?

options.A: An extra pair of clean examination gloves
options.B: A spare blood pressure cuff and stethoscope
options.C: A quick source of sugar like glucose tablets
options.D: A bottle of surgical rubbing alcohol

explanation: Hypoglycemia can strike anywhere. Having glucose tablets or sweets on hand lets the patient treat a sudden crash immediately.

question: Why should you avoid pouring harsh surgical scrubs directly inside an open wound?

options.A: It can damage exposed tissue cells and delay proper wound healing
options.B: It instantly inactivates any local anesthetic you inject later
options.C: It permanently stains the surrounding skin a bright yellow color
options.D: It causes the skin edges to swell up and prevent knot tying

explanation: Harsh chemicals are too strong for delicate exposed cells inside a wound. Stick to normal saline for cleaning—your patients will heal much better!

question: Why would a doctor order a pelvic ultrasound for a patient with a suspected incomplete abortion?

options.A: To check the patient's blood group and crossmatch
options.B: To measure hormone levels in the kidneys
options.C: To check for leftover pregnancy tissue in the uterus
options.D: To count the exact white blood cells in the body

explanation: An ultrasound lets the team peek inside the womb to confirm if any pregnancy tissue is still trapped. Super helpful diagnostic tool!

question: What is the primary reason nurses perform frequent neurovascular checks on a casted limb?

options.A: To clean away dead skin cells accumulating under the bandage
options.B: To catch early signs of impaired circulation and nerve damage
options.C: To measure how fast the bone is knitting back together
options.D: To determine the exact weight of the plaster cast material

explanation: Checking pulses, color, warmth, and feeling helps you catch circulation problems or nerve compression before permanent damage sets in.

question: Which part of the large intestine does a sigmoidoscopy check?

options.A: The lower third, including the rectum and sigmoid colon
options.B: The entire length of the large intestine
options.C: The cecum and appendix only
options.D: Only the transverse and ascending colon

explanation: You've got this! A sigmoidoscopy focuses specifically on the lower part of the bowel (rectum and sigmoid colon), unlike a full colonoscopy which looks at the whole length.

question: At what total GCS score do clinicians usually start preparing to intubate and protect the patient's airway?

options.A: 12 or lower
options.B: 8 or lower
options.C: 14 or lower
options.D: 10 or lower

explanation: As nurses say in the emergency unit: 'Less than 8, intubate!' A score of 8 or lower usually means the patient can't protect their own airway.

question: What metal is most commonly used to manufacture standard surgical instruments?

options.A: Stainless steel
options.B: Pure copper
options.C: Soft brass
options.D: Cast aluminum

explanation: Stainless steel is chosen because it resists rust and can survive the high temperatures of repeated sterilization cycles. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h1)

question: What is the very first action a nurse should take with a surgical instrument immediately after a procedure is finished?

options.A: Wrap it tightly in sterile cloth for storage
options.B: Soak the instrument in strong bleach overnight
options.C: Place it directly into the clean instrument cabinet
options.D: Remove gross soil and blood to prevent drying

explanation: Wiping off heavy blood and tissue right away keeps it from drying onto the metal, which makes later cleaning much harder. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h5)

question: Which infection is a nurse most afraid of contracting after an accidental needle stick injury?

options.A: Tuberculosis
options.B: Cholera
options.C: Hepatitis B
options.D: Malaria

explanation: That's right! Blood-borne viruses like Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and HIV are our biggest concerns after a sharp injury.

question: Why do smartphones and social media apps increase the risk of early unprotected sex?

options.A: They automatically increase hormone production in the adolescent brain
options.B: They allow teens to easily find partners and arrange secret meetings away from adult supervision
options.C: They replace comprehensive sex education with verified medical facts
options.D: They prevent teenagers from communicating with their peers

explanation: Digital technology provides private channels for teens to connect, flirt, and arrange hookups without parents or teachers knowing. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h7)

question: Why would you choose a subcutaneous injection instead of an IV for certain drugs like insulin?

options.A: To make the drug work instantly throughout the body
options.B: To bypass the need for a sterile syringe
options.C: To prevent any local skin irritation
options.D: To achieve a slow, sustained absorption rate

explanation: Spot on! Fatty tissue has fewer blood vessels than veins or muscles, which helps drugs like insulin release slowly and steadily into the body.

question: Why is watching a patient walk (their gait) such an important part of a nursing assessment?

options.A: It replaces the need to check vital signs during an admission
options.B: It measures the exact level of calcium circulating in the blood
options.C: It provides a definitive laboratory diagnosis for osteoporosis
options.D: It reveals hidden balance issues and weaknesses in weight-bearing joints

explanation: A quick look at how someone walks can tell you a lot about their balance and joint strength before they take a nasty fall!

question: What actually causes that sharp, terrible pain and swelling during a gout flare?

options.A: Complete wearing away of the cartilage
options.B: Sudden thickening of the synovial fluid
options.C: Uric acid crystals building up in the joint
options.D: A bacterial infection inside the joint capsule

explanation: You've got this! When uric acid piles up, it forms needle-like crystals in the joint. Your body's immune system attacks these crystals, leading to that fiery pain and swelling.

question: How is cancer grading different from cancer staging?

options.A: Grading counts white blood cells, while staging counts red blood cells
options.B: Grading is only used for benign tumors, while staging is for malignant ones
options.C: Grading looks at cellular appearance under a microscope, while staging looks at how far the cancer has spread
options.D: Grading measures organ failure, while staging measures treatment success

explanation: Think of it this way: Grading checks how 'wild' or abnormal the cells look under a microscope, while staging looks at the map of the body to see how far the cancer has traveled.

question: Which of the following does NOT falsely alter a fasting blood sugar result?

options.A: Experiencing emotional or physical stress
options.B: Fasting for longer than 14 hours
options.C: Taking steroid medications in the morning
options.D: Drinking plain water during the fast

explanation: Plain water is totally fine! It has no sugar or calories, so drinking it won't ruin your patient's lab test.

question: What happens when a patient lacks essential haematinics?

options.A: Red blood cell production is impaired
options.B: White blood cells multiply uncontrollably
options.C: Platelets aggregate too quickly in vessels
options.D: The heart slows down its pumping rate

explanation: Without raw materials like iron, the bone marrow simply doesn't have what it needs to pump out enough red blood cells. Great job connecting the dots!

question: How do you deflate the retention balloon before taking out a Foley catheter?

options.A: Puncture the outer catheter wall with a large needle
options.B: Cut the balloon valve tubing with surgical scissors
options.C: Inject more water to pop the balloon safely inside the bladder
options.D: Attach a syringe to the inflation port and draw out all the water

explanation: Spot on! Hooking up a syringe and pulling out the exact amount of water that was put in ensures the balloon collapses completely before you slide the tube out.

question: Why is pulling your mask down around your neck during a break a bad idea?

options.A: It violates fashion codes
options.B: It stretches out the elastic bands forever
options.C: It contaminates the clean inside of your mask with germs from your neck skin
options.D: It blocks blood flow to your head

explanation: Pulling it to your neck exposes the inner lining to skin oils and germs, which you then breathe right back in!

question: When a mother of young children is admitted to the hospital for major surgery, what is the most likely effect on her family?

options.A: Family members will immediately stop working to stay in the hospital room.
options.B: Household expenses will decrease due to reduced grocery shopping.
options.C: The family structure remains entirely unchanged during hospital stays.
options.D: Family roles must be rearranged to cover childcare and household duties.

explanation: Spot on! When a key caregiver falls ill, family routines get disrupted, forcing other members to step up and handle chores and childcare.

question: Which medication is typically prescribed as the first-line oral treatment for Type 2 diabetes?

options.A: Regular insulin
options.B: NPH insulin
options.C: Metformin
options.D: Glibenclamide

explanation: Metformin is universally recommended as the starting oral drug because it lowers blood sugar effectively without causing weight gain or low blood sugar on its own. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h4)

question: A patient with severe tummy pain walks into the clinic bent forward. What is causing this posture?

options.A: Normal aging changes
options.B: A neurological stroke
options.C: Extreme psychological joy
options.D: Pain and guarding

explanation: This is called 'guarding.' It's a natural, protective reflex where the body curls inward to shield a painful spot from touch or stretch.

question: Which symptom is most common in perinatal anxiety disorders during pregnancy?

options.A: Sudden temporary loss of long-term memory
options.B: Complete indifference toward the entire pregnancy process
options.C: Physical weight gain without any emotional changes
options.D: Excessive, hard-to-control worry about the baby's health

explanation: Correct! Perinatal anxiety often looks like persistent, overwhelming fear and worry regarding the baby's safety.

question: After a diagnostic laparoscopy, a patient complains of sharp shoulder pain. What is likely going on?

options.A: Severe emotional anxiety manifesting as physical upper body tension
options.B: A torn shoulder muscle from positioning on the operating table
options.C: Residual carbon dioxide gas irritating the diaphragm
options.D: An allergic reaction to the skin antiseptic applied before surgery

explanation: Correct! The gas used to puff up the tummy during surgery can drift up and irritate the diaphragm, causing a weird referred pain in the shoulder. It passes soon!

question: An alert and oriented older patient refuses a recommended medical treatment, but their adult children demand that the nurse force the treatment. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately without further discussion.
options.B: Administer the treatment secretly in the patient's food.
options.C: Follow the children's wishes because they are family members.
options.D: Respect the patient's refusal because they have autonomy and capacity.

explanation: An adult with decision-making capacity has the legal and ethical right to accept or refuse treatment, regardless of family opinions. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T1#GNS321_U3_T1_h6)

question: What term is used when people delay or refuse vaccines even though they are available?

options.A: Herd immunity
options.B: Vaccine hesitancy
options.C: Cold chain failure
options.D: Antigen fatigue

explanation: Spot on! 'Vaccine hesitancy' describes when people feel unsure or hold back from getting vaccinated due to various doubts or worries.

question: What is the main reason our bodies have cavities protecting internal organs?

options.A: To produce blood cells for the immune system
options.B: To increase total body weight and maintain posture
options.C: To safeguard delicate internal organs from physical trauma
options.D: To control the rate of voluntary muscle movement

explanation: Body cavities act as natural physical shields that enclose and protect your vital organs from sudden bumps and movements.

question: What is the main reason a nursing student is in the operating theatre?

options.A: To administer anaesthetic medications independently
options.B: To replace the scrub nurse during complex procedures
options.C: To act as the primary circulating nurse for major cases
options.D: To learn and observe surgical nursing care firsthand

explanation: As a student, you are there to gain experience, connect your classroom notes to real-life practice, and learn safely under supervision!

question: What happens to a patient's metabolic rate during severe physiological stress like major trauma or sepsis?

options.A: It remains completely unchanged
options.B: It fluctuates only during sleep
options.C: It drops to zero instantly
options.D: It increases significantly

explanation: Severe physical trauma and infections trigger a hypermetabolic state that dramatically increases energy expenditure. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T008#GNS227_U4_T008_h7)

question: What happens inside cells when they go without oxygen for too long (prolonged ischemia)?

options.A: They stop producing waste products entirely to save energy.
options.B: They begin storing large amounts of extra oxygen for later use.
options.C: They switch to anaerobic metabolism and produce excess lactic acid.
options.D: They rapidly multiply to replace the damaged surrounding tissue.

explanation: Without oxygen, cells panic a bit and switch to backup mode (anaerobic metabolism). This backup creates extra lactic acid, which causes that familiar ache.

question: How would you describe a delusion?

options.A: A complete lack of emotional expression
options.B: A fixed, false belief resistant to logic
options.C: A sudden inability to speak any words
options.D: A sensory experience without external stimuli

explanation: Well done! A delusion is a strong belief that stays stuck in the person's mind, even when clear facts show it isn't true.

question: In the handy PQRSTU pain assessment tool, what does the letter 'Q' stand for?

options.A: Quietness
options.B: Quantity
options.C: Quickness
options.D: Quality

explanation: Easy peasy! 'Q' stands for quality—asking the patient what the pain actually *feels* like (e.g., stabbing, dull, aching, or burning).

question: What is the main job of hepatocytes inside the liver?

options.A: Producing red blood cells
options.B: Handling metabolism and clearing out toxins
options.C: Pumping oxygenated blood into the systemic circulation
options.D: Filtering waste through the kidneys

explanation: Hepatocytes are the hardworking main cells of the liver. They manage your metabolism, build proteins, and clear out body toxins every single day!

question: Which simple non-pharmacological nursing intervention often helps relieve sudden breathlessness?

options.A: Placing the patient flat on their back without a pillow
options.B: Closing all windows and doors to trap warm indoor air
options.C: Asking the patient to hold their breath for one minute
options.D: Directing a cool fan or breeze across the patient's face

explanation: Stimulating the trigeminal nerve with cool airflow helps trick the brain into feeling like breathing is easier. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T15#GNS321_U4_T15_h4)

question: What is the most common and preferred site for giving an intradermal injection?

options.A: Upper outer quadrant of the buttock
options.B: Volar surface of the forearm
options.C: Deltoid muscle of the upper arm
options.D: Anterior thigh muscle

explanation: Spot on! The inner forearm is easy to reach, has very little hair, and lets you clearly see any skin reactions.

question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of normal wound healing that a patient should expect?

options.A: A thin line of pinkness near the cut
options.B: Pus draining from the incision site
options.C: Dry scabbing along the suture line
options.D: Mild tenderness around the edges

question: Why might a community want smaller families on average, yet still have a low Contraceptive Prevalence Rate?

options.A: Excessive availability of free clinical staff in every village
options.B: Systemic barriers like supply stock-outs and spousal opposition
options.C: Natural biological immunity to pregnancy in rural populations
options.D: Universal rejection of modern medicine by community elders

explanation: Wanting a smaller family is one thing, but if clinics run out of supplies or partners object, women can't access the protection they want.

question: What is the core problem happening inside the body during clinical shock?

options.A: Widespread inadequate cellular perfusion throughout the body
options.B: An excessive buildup of red blood cells inside the heart
options.C: A sudden and permanent drop in body temperature only
options.D: Local inflammation confined strictly to superficial skin veins

explanation: Shock is a medical emergency where the whole circulatory system fails to deliver enough blood and oxygen to keep the body's tissues happy and alive.

question: Why is family planning counseling especially important for a grand multiparous mother after she gives birth?

options.A: Having more pregnancies carries higher health risks for both mother and baby.
options.B: Contraceptives completely eliminate the risk of postpartum depression.
options.C: She will automatically lose the ability to breastfeed future infants.
options.D: Her legal right to bear children is restricted by hospital policy.

explanation: Good counseling helps parents understand how risks stack up with each new pregnancy, empowering them to make the best choices for spacing or finishing their family.

question: Which bacterium causes General Paralysis of the Insane (GPI)?

options.A: Neisseria meningitidis
options.B: Treponema pallidum
options.C: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
options.D: Streptococcus pneumoniae

explanation: You got this! GPI is a serious neurological condition that happens when a syphilis infection caused by Treponema pallidum is left untreated for a long time.

question: Which two brain chemicals are mainly responsible for balancing excitation and inhibition?

options.A: Acetylcholine and epinephrine
options.B: Dopamine and serotonin
options.C: Norepinephrine and histamine
options.D: Glutamate and GABA

explanation: Think of glutamate as the gas pedal (excitatory) and GABA as the brake pedal (inhibitory). Keeping them balanced keeps the brain stable!

question: When a heart valve is narrowed and blocked, what kind of extra strain does it put on the heart?

options.A: Electrical overload
options.B: Perfusion overload
options.C: Volume overload
options.D: Pressure overload

explanation: When a valve is narrowed, the heart has to push much harder to squeeze blood through it. That extra resistance creates a pressure overload!

question: In simple terms, what is atelectasis?

options.A: An abnormal collection of air in the pleural cavity
options.B: A severe bacterial infection inside the lung tissue
options.C: The collapse or closure of a lung resulting in reduced gas exchange
options.D: High pressure inside the blood vessels of the lungs

explanation: Correct! Atelectasis happens when tiny air sacs (alveoli) deflate or collapse, making it harder to trade gases.

question: Which condition is the most common immediate complication following a thoracocentesis?

options.A: Acute liver damage
options.B: Pneumothorax
options.C: Pulmonary embolism
options.D: Severe kidney failure

explanation: Accidental puncture of the lung surface allows air to enter the pleural space, resulting in a pneumothorax. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T17#GNS221_U2_T17_h7)

question: What is the main job of activated charcoal when given for something a patient swallowed?

options.A: To neutralize stomach acid and prevent internal bleeding
options.B: To bind toxins in the gut and prevent them from entering the blood
options.C: To coat the throat and protect it from corrosive chemicals
options.D: To cause immediate vomiting and empty the stomach contents

explanation: Activated charcoal acts like a tiny sponge in the stomach! It grabs onto the toxins so they pass safely out of the body instead of entering the bloodstream.

question: Which type of heart tumour do nurses see more often in clinical practice?

options.A: Primary papillary fibroelastomas
options.B: Primary malignant sarcomas
options.C: Congenital rhabdomyomas
options.D: Secondary metastatic tumours

explanation: Cancers that travel to the heart from other parts of the body (metastatic tumours) actually happen much more often than tumours that start directly in the heart tissue. Everyday nursing knowledge!

question: What is the primary purpose of performing a standard 12-lead ECG?

options.A: To remove dangerous blood clots in arteries
options.B: To record the electrical activity of the heart
options.C: To check the levels of oxygen in the veins
options.D: To measure the exact amount of blood pumped

explanation: An ECG traces the electrical impulses moving through the heart muscle to identify rhythm problems and ischemic damage. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T2#GNS213_U1_T2_h5)

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team essential in palliative symptom management?

options.A: Doctors are not allowed to speak directly with family members
options.B: Complex physical and emotional symptoms require varied professional expertise
options.C: Hospital regulations state that five nurses must see every patient
options.D: It prevents nurses from having to perform any physical assessments

explanation: No single discipline can address every physical, psychological, and spiritual need of a dying patient. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T15#GNS321_U4_T15_h8)

question: What is the main purpose of the foramen ovale in a baby's heart before birth?

options.A: Connecting the umbilical vein to the inferior vena cava to bypass the liver
options.B: Allowing blood to flow from the right atrium directly into the left atrium
options.C: Preventing maternal blood cells from entering the foetal heart chambers
options.D: Directing deoxygenated blood from the upper body back to the placenta

explanation: Spot on! The foramen ovale is a little flap-like door between the heart's upper chambers that lets oxygen-rich blood skip the right ventricle and lungs. You're doing brilliantly!

question: Which nursing action helps build instant trust with a newly admitted PAC patient?

options.A: Reviewing the client's chart at the nursing station before entering
options.B: Asking the client to sign financial clearance forms immediately
options.C: Instructing visitors to leave the ward before nursing assessment begins
options.D: Explaining every clinical procedure clearly before touching the client

explanation: Telling her what you are about to do shows deep respect for her body and eases the fear of feeling helpless in the hospital.

question: When is the risk of getting pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) highest after an IUD insertion?

options.A: Only if the client gets pregnant with the IUD
options.B: During the first 20 days after insertion
options.C: There is never any risk of infection
options.D: After the IUD has been in place for five years

explanation: Because tiny amounts of bacteria can accidentally enter the uterus during the procedure, the infection risk is highest right after insertion, during the first few weeks.

question: What are the two main components that make up the cardiovascular system?

options.A: The brain and spinal cord
options.B: The heart and blood vessels
options.C: The lungs and airways
options.D: The kidneys and bladder

explanation: The cardiovascular system is composed of the heart, which acts as the pump, and blood vessels, which serve as the delivery pipes. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why do patients with Addison's disease need to take higher doses of their steroid medication when they are sick or stressed?

options.A: The body normally increases cortisol output during stress, and these patients cannot produce their own.
options.B: Increased steroids prevent the kidneys from excreting too much sodium and water.
options.C: Higher doses of steroids are required to kill off invading bacteria during an infection.
options.D: Infection destroys oral medications faster in the stomach, requiring higher amounts to reach the blood.

explanation: Healthy bodies naturally make extra cortisol when fighting off illness. Since Addison's patients can't make their own backup supply, they must take extra pills to help their body cope safely.

question: As a nurse, what is the main goal of gender-transformative healthcare?

options.A: To prevent teenagers from ever talking about relationships
options.B: To focus exclusively on male patients during clinic hours
options.C: To actively challenge harmful norms while improving health access
options.D: To enforce traditional cultural rules inside hospital wards

explanation: Brilliant! This approach doesn't just treat the medical issue; it tackles the underlying social unfairness causing the health problem in the first place.

question: What happens if a nurse forgets to push the foreskin back down after cleaning an uncircumcised male patient?

options.A: Paraphimosis and painful swelling of the penis
options.B: Permanent loss of bladder control
options.C: Total blockage of urine flow
options.D: A fast fungal infection on the legs

explanation: Spot on! Leaving the foreskin pulled back acts like a tight rope, cutting off blood flow and causing a painful swelling called paraphimosis.

question: What is the modern medical approach to non-urgent surgeries on intersex infants?

options.A: Delaying non-urgent procedures to protect bodily autonomy until the child can participate
options.B: Mandating hormone therapy immediately after birth
options.C: Ignoring the physical variation completely without any documentation
options.D: Performing immediate surgery on every infant to fix chromosomal imbalances

explanation: You got it! Modern medical ethics value a child's right to their own body, avoiding rushed, irreversible cosmetic surgeries.

question: What is the name of the mature, fluid-filled follicle ready for release?

options.A: Primordial follicle
options.B: Corpus albicans
options.C: Graafian follicle
options.D: Atretic follicle

explanation: The Graafian follicle is the final, large, fluid-filled stage of follicular development that ruptures during ovulation. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which nursing diagnosis fits best for a patient struggling with painful bladder spasms and trouble urinating due to an enlarged prostate?

options.A: Impaired urinary elimination
options.B: Risk for impaired skin integrity
options.C: Ineffective tissue perfusion
options.D: Excess fluid volume

explanation: An enlarged prostate blocks the normal flow of urine, directly leading to an alteration in urinary elimination. Perfect match for the nursing care plan!

question: What role do prostaglandins play when someone develops a fever?

options.A: They attack and destroy bacteria in the blood
options.B: They relax muscles to stop shivering
options.C: They turn on sweat glands to cool the skin
options.D: They tell the hypothalamus to raise the body's temperature setting

explanation: You're doing great! Prostaglandins act like messengers telling your brain's thermostat to crank up the heat.

question: What is the main job of T-tubules during muscle contraction?

options.A: They produce the ATP required for cross-bridge cycling
options.B: They store calcium ions until a contraction begins
options.C: They carry the electrical action potential deep into the muscle fiber
options.D: They anchor thin actin filaments to the Z-lines

explanation: Think of T-tubules as underground tunnels that carry surface electrical signals straight to the deep core of the muscle cell so everything contracts together. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h4)

question: Which emotional reaction is a patient facing a terminal diagnosis most likely to experience first?

options.A: Complete emotional numbness
options.B: Relief from daily stress
options.C: Peaceful acceptance
options.D: Denial and shock

explanation: Denial is a common initial defense mechanism that helps protect the psyche from being overwhelmed by catastrophic news. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T13#GNS321_U4_T13_h3)

question: Where does radioactive hospital waste usually come from?

options.A: Nuclear medicine and radiotherapy units
options.B: Administrative records and billing offices
options.C: General outpatient consulting rooms
options.D: Hospital kitchens and dining areas

explanation: Right on target! Radioactive materials are strictly used in specialized departments like cancer treatment and imaging. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T2#GNS122_U5_T2_h6)

question: What is a big benefit of using digital inventory systems instead of paper records?

options.A: It ensures clinical injections never cause skin pain
options.B: It completely stops nurses from ever needing to count items
options.C: It lets central managers view stock data across sites quickly
options.D: It stops medical supplies from reaching their expiration date

explanation: Spot on! Digital systems link different clinics together, making it super easy to spot trends and shortages early.

question: Which of the following describes the difference between macronutrients and micronutrients?

options.A: Micronutrients are digested much faster than any macronutrient
options.B: Micronutrients are needed in smaller amounts and do not provide direct calories
options.C: Macronutrients are stored in bones while micronutrients float in blood
options.D: Macronutrients are only needed during childhood and growth phases

explanation: While macronutrients are consumed in large amounts for energy and structure, micronutrients are needed in tiny amounts to regulate body processes without supplying calories. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T015#GNS227_U2_T015_h3)

question: What is a major viral infection linked closely to cervical cancer in Nigeria?

options.A: Human Immunodeficiency Virus
options.B: Hepatitis B virus
options.C: Epstein-Barr virus
options.D: Human Papillomavirus

explanation: Persistent infection with high-risk strains of Human Papillomavirus is the primary driver behind most cervical cancer cases. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h2)

question: What should a nurse do when a woman in labor develops a complication too severe for a primary health clinic?

options.A: Quickly arrange a safe transfer to a higher-level facility with CEmONC
options.B: Wait until morning to see if she gets better
options.C: Try to perform surgery right there without proper tools
options.D: Tell the family to take her home for local herbs

explanation: Brilliant! Prompt referral saves lives when your clinic lacks the surgery and blood transfusion resources needed for severe emergencies.

question: Where is compact bone primarily found in the human skeleton?

options.A: The outer shell of bones
options.B: The inner core of short bones
options.C: The center of the marrow cavity
options.D: The tips of growing joints

explanation: Spot on! Compact bone forms the tough, solid outer shell of your bones. It acts like heavy armor, protecting the inner parts and giving your body the strength to stand and move.

question: An endometrioma happens when which of the following occurs?

options.A: Ovarian surface cells multiply and produce thick mucus
options.B: The corpus luteum traps blood inside its cavity after ovulation
options.C: Uterine lining tissue grows on the outside of the ovary
options.D: An unruptured egg follicle swells excessively with clear fluid

explanation: Think of endometriomas (often called chocolate cysts!) as happening when tissue similar to the lining of the uterus decides to grow outside on the ovaries.

question: Why might some patients with cervical irritation feel absolutely no symptoms at all?

options.A: The inflammatory process can remain mild and localized without triggering pain receptors.
options.B: Hormones in the vagina completely block any physical sensation of swelling.
options.C: The body instantly neutralizes all bacterial toxins before they reach the surface.
options.D: Nerve endings in the cervix are purely motor and never transmit sensory signals.

explanation: Exactly! Mild inflammation often stays quiet without setting off pain signals, which is why regular screening tests are so important for women's health.

question: When washing a patient's arms or legs during a bed bath, why does the nurse stroke from the hands or feet toward the torso?

options.A: To check if the patient has broken bones in the hand
options.B: To push all dirt and sweat directly into the armpits
options.C: To make the skin stretch out and look younger
options.D: To promote venous blood return toward the heart

explanation: Brilliant! Moving your washcloth upward helps push venous blood back up toward the heart against gravity, which is great for circulation.

question: What is dyspareunia, a common complaint among FGM survivors?

options.A: Severe fear of hospital environments
options.B: Chronic swelling of the lower legs
options.C: Inability to produce breast milk
options.D: Painful sexual intercourse

explanation: Dyspareunia simply means persistent pain during sex, usually resulting from severe scarring and nerve damage. Knowing this helps you support your patients better!

question: What complex surgery involves removing the head of the pancreas, the duodenum, and the gallbladder?

options.A: Whipple procedure
options.B: Cholecystostomy
options.C: Splenectomy
options.D: Gastric bypass

explanation: The Whipple procedure is a major operation performed to treat tumors located in the head of the pancreas. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h7)

question: Which type of drink should patients avoid right after a tonsillectomy so you can easily spot if they are bleeding?

options.A: Clear water
options.B: Apple juice
options.C: Plain milk
options.D: Red-colored fluids

explanation: You got it! We avoid red drinks because if the patient vomits or spits up, the red color looks just like fresh blood and can easily cause a false alarm (or hide real bleeding).

question: What is a crucial safety rule to remember when giving a therapeutic or medicated bath?

options.A: Leaving the patient completely unattended so they can relax
options.B: Making the water as hot as possible to open up the pores fully
options.C: Avoiding the use of any towels after the patient steps out
options.D: Limiting the bath duration to prevent skin maceration and exhaustion

explanation: Remember, soaking too long can waterlog fragile skin and totally wear out a patient who is already weak from illness. Keep an eye on the clock!

question: Which part of the male urethra is the widest and passes straight through the prostate gland?

options.A: Preprostatic segment
options.B: Spongy segment
options.C: Prostatic segment
options.D: Membranous segment

explanation: Well done! The prostatic urethra gets its name because it is snugly encased by the prostate gland.

question: Where in the digestive tract do most oral drugs actually get absorbed into the body?

options.A: The small intestine
options.B: The esophagus
options.C: The stomach
options.D: The large intestine

explanation: The small intestine is the champion of absorption! With its massive surface area covered in tiny villi, it's the main highway for drugs to enter the bloodstream.

question: Which lifestyle habit is a known trigger that worsens inflammation in rheumatic conditions?

options.A: Eating fresh green vegetables
options.B: Walking short distances daily
options.C: Smoking cigarettes
options.D: Drinking too much clean water

explanation: Tobacco smoke contains chemicals that fire up the immune system and make inflammation much worse, especially in conditions like rheumatoid arthritis.

question: What clinic setup helps reduce anxiety and shyness for young people seeking care?

options.A: Sharing waiting rooms with adult surgical patients
options.B: Mandatory parental accompaniment for everyone
options.C: Dedicated operating hours specifically for youth
options.D: Strict appointment booking months in advance

explanation: You got it! Special youth hours let adolescents feel less conspicuous and more relaxed among their peers.

question: Which medication class is well-known for causing severe constipation as a side effect?

options.A: Broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: Opioid pain relievers
options.C: Short-acting diuretics
options.D: Inhaled bronchodilators

explanation: Opioids slow down the movement of the gastrointestinal tract significantly, leading to hard, difficult-to-pass stool. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h2)

question: Why do pre-existing medical conditions often get worse during pregnancy?

options.A: Pregnancy significantly increases the workload on the mother's heart, lungs, and kidneys
options.B: Metabolic rates drop drastically to conserve energy for the developing baby
options.C: Hormonal surges permanently deactivate prescribed medications in the bloodstream
options.D: The growing fetus directly consumes all of the mother's circulating red blood cells

explanation: The body experiences a massive increase in blood volume and cardiac output to support the baby, which puts extra stress on organs that were already struggling. You're mastering maternal physiology!

question: Why do doctors order cardiac enzyme blood tests for a patient with severe chest pain?

options.A: To measure how fast red blood cells are moving
options.B: To test the liver's ability to process fats
options.C: To find out if the patient has a bacterial infection
options.D: To check if heart muscle tissue has been injured

explanation: When heart cells die from lack of oxygen, they release specific enzymes into the bloodstream, confirming a heart attack. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T2#GNS213_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is usually the very first sign of puerperal sepsis in a new mother?

options.A: Hair loss
options.B: Constipation
options.C: Weight gain
options.D: Fever

explanation: Always watch out for temperature spikes! A sudden fever is typically the earliest and most important warning sign that an infection is brewing postpartum.

question: How does dopamine affect the indirect pathway to help us move?

options.A: It activates the indirect pathway to freeze all motor actions
options.B: It suppresses the indirect pathway to reduce braking on movement
options.C: It turns dopamine into acetylcholine
options.D: It destroys the subthalamic nucleus immediately

explanation: Think of the indirect pathway as a brake on your movements. Dopamine steps on the gas (direct pathway) and eases off the brakes (indirect pathway), making it smooth and easy for you to move!

question: Why is cancer staging so important after a patient receives a confirmed diagnosis?

options.A: It guides treatment decisions and helps determine the overall prognosis
options.B: It identifies the exact environmental toxin that caused the disease
options.C: It guarantees that the patient will achieve full remission
options.D: It completely replaces the need for any laboratory blood tests

explanation: You got it! Staging lets the team know how far the cancer has spread, which helps them choose the best treatment plan and understand what lies ahead.

question: A nurse is caring for a patient with a surgical wound. Which finding suggests the local inflammation is worsening into a serious infection?

options.A: A slight drop in blood pressure after getting out of bed
options.B: Mild itching directly over the healing scar line
options.C: Normal skin color surrounding the closed surgical staples
options.D: Pus drainage and spreading redness around the incision

explanation: Purulent drainage and expanding erythema are classic clinical indicators of worsening infection in a wound. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h6)

question: What prompted the creation of formal critical care nursing organizations and certification standards?

options.A: The complete elimination of physicians from intensive care units
options.B: A government mandate to reduce the total number of working hospital nurses
options.C: The increasing complexity of patient technology requiring advanced specialized skills
options.D: A sudden drop in the number of students applying to nursing school

explanation: General training could not keep pace with advanced monitors and life support, leading to the creation of specialized critical care nursing standards. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why does damaged joint cartilage take such a long time to heal?

options.A: It lacks a direct blood supply
options.B: It is constantly dissolved by joint fluid
options.C: It has too many active breakdown cells
options.D: It contains no cells at all

explanation: Because cartilage doesn't have its own blood vessels, healing nutrients have to slowly ooze in from nearby tissues, making repair a very slow process.

question: What is the main goal of using skull traction for someone with a neck injury?

options.A: To align and stabilize damaged cervical vertebrae
options.B: To completely replace the need for future spinal surgery
options.C: To deliver intravenous pain medication directly to the neck
options.D: To increase blood flow to the brain tissues

explanation: You've got this! Skull traction gently pulls to put broken or dislocated neck bones back into place and keeps them steady so they can heal safely.

question: What is the main goal of pharmacovigilance in healthcare?

options.A: Marketing new pharmaceutical products to regional hospitals
options.B: Detecting, assessing, and preventing adverse drug effects
options.C: Speeding up the clinical drug trial approval process
options.D: Calculating the financial cost of manufactured medications

explanation: Pharmacovigilance is the ongoing safety monitoring process designed to catch and prevent drug-related harm. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h8)

question: A patient with large fibroids complains of constant tiredness, pale skin, and dizziness during her heavy periods. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Hormonal imbalance stopping ovulation completely
options.B: A sudden severe pelvic infection
options.C: Iron-deficiency anemia from chronic blood loss
options.D: Complete blockage of the cervix by scar tissue

explanation: Spot on! Losing a lot of blood month after month depletes the body's iron stores, leading to classic anemia symptoms like fatigue and paleness.

question: What is a crucial teaching point for someone prescribed an epinephrine auto-injector for severe allergies?

options.A: Keep the device stored inside a kitchen refrigerator at all times
options.B: Demonstrate how to self-administer the device into the outer thigh and call emergency services
options.C: Use the auto-injector only after taking oral antihistamines first
options.D: Replace the device once every ten years regardless of expiration date

explanation: Make sure your patient knows how to jab that auto-injector firmly into their outer thigh, and remind them to always call for emergency help right after!

question: What does a susceptible host represent in the chain of infection?

options.A: A medical instrument sterilized prior to a procedure
options.B: A person who lacks resistance to a specific pathogen
options.C: The physical surface where bacteria live and multiply
options.D: The specific pathway a virus uses to leave the body

explanation: A susceptible host is an individual whose immune system is weak or compromised enough to allow an infection to take hold. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h2)

question: The main cause of hematuria investigated by an IVP is...

options.A: low white blood cell count in blood
options.B: blood present in the urine sample
options.C: elevated fasting blood sugar levels
options.D: excessive fluid intake during meals

explanation: Hematuria simply means blood in the urine, and an IVP helps find where that bleeding is originating along the urinary tract. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is the main trigger for cancer starting in the body?

options.A: Genetic mutations that cause uncontrolled cell division
options.B: Overgrowth of normal flora inside the renal pelvis
options.C: A sudden decrease in daily fluid intake and hydration
options.D: Temporary blockages in the main ureter passageways

explanation: Cancer begins when changes happen in cellular DNA. Normally, cells grow and die in an orderly way, but mutations tell them to keep dividing without stopping.

question: As a nurse or rescuer, what is the very first thing you must check at an emergency scene?

options.A: Ensure the safety of the surrounding environment
options.B: Check the patient's blood pressure
options.C: Administer intravenous medications
options.D: Begin chest compressions immediately

explanation: Safety first! Always check for dangers (like live wires or smoke) so you don't become a second victim needing rescue.
